question: Delamination claims are up - what's going on?

guard_decision.reason: The question asks to investigate delamination warranty claims, which is directly measurable via the delamination_claim_rate metric. While the question doesn't specify a time window or grouping, the reasonable default is to investigate the most recent data using the metric's available dimensions (batch, press_line, or month grain) to surface patterns explaining the increase.

metrics.name: delamination_claim_rate
metrics.definition: Warranty claims with defect_type "delamination" per 100 decks, counted only among decks that have reached 90 days of field maturity (90 days since ship_date as of the metric's as-of date). Decks younger than 90 days are excluded from both the numerator and the denominator.

metrics.name: first_pass_yield
metrics.definition: The share of decks in a production batch that pass quality inspection on the first inspection, with no rework or reprocessing. Computed as decks passing first inspection divided by total decks inspected in the batch.

metrics.name: on_time_ship_rate
metrics.definition: The share of orders shipped on or before their committed ship date (order_date plus standard lead time), out of all orders with a non-cancelled status.

metrics.name: scrap_cost_per_batch
metrics.definition: Total material and labor cost attributed to decks scrapped during production for a batch, divided by the batch's planned deck count. Scrap is any deck that fails inspection and is not reworked.

metrics.name: veneer_yield
metrics.definition: The fraction of a maple veneer material lot's received quantity that is actually drawn into production batches, versus left unused as remainder or trim. Computed as the sum of quantity_used across every batch that consumes the lot, divided by the lot's received quantity.

result.definition: Warranty claims with defect_type "delamination" per 100 decks, counted only among decks that have reached 90 days of field maturity (90 days since ship_date as of the metric's as-of date). Decks younger than 90 days are excluded from both the numerator and the denominator.
result.rationale: Delamination is a defect that surfaces with use, not at the moment of sale — a deck typically has to be ridden, get wet, and take a few impacts before a sub-par adhesive bond starts to show itself. A metric of raw claims over decks shipped is biased toward whichever batches are oldest, because they have had the most time to accumulate claims, and it is biased against the newest batches, which look artificially safe simply because they have not been skated long enough to start to fail. That makes "raw claims over shipped" actively misleading during exactly the window when catching a bad batch matters most: a newly-discovered material problem would look clean under that definition for months, by which time far more decks have shipped. Matching on maturity — comparing batches only once each has had the same amount of field time — is what makes the batches comparable at all, and it is the difference between "we have a lot problem" and "we have a plausible pattern that might just be an aging artifact."

final_answer:
## Summary

**Delamination claim rate** (warranty claims with defect_type "delamination" per 100 decks, counted only among decks that have reached 90 days of field maturity) has drifted up over the last several months — monthly readings of ~2.0–2.9 in Oct/Nov 2025 and Jan/Feb/May 2026 versus a baseline of ~1.0–1.6 earlier in 2025. (Note: batches B0050, B0203, B0233 are excluded from all these readings because they already have an approved quarantine action.)

At the batch level, the picture isn't a single across-the-board rise — it's driven by a tail of specific batches with unusually high rates (up to 10 claims/100 decks) sitting far above the rest, which mostly read 0. I anchored on the single most extreme batch, **B0049** (10.0/100), and traversed its consumed material lots and press line. Its maple veneer lot (LOT-MAP-005) and press line (PL03) didn't recur among the other high-rate batches, and its epoxy resin lot (LOT-EPO-012) turned out to be used by essentially every batch I checked — including all-zero-claim ones — so that's a generic, fleet-wide input and not a meaningful signal on its own.

Widening to the next tier of elevated batches turned up a cleaner pattern: **B0030 (9.68), B0069 (9.09), and B0002 (8.70)** all consume the same maple veneer lot, **LOT-MAP-007**, received 2025-08-16 from supplier **SUP02**. That lot did not appear in any of the zero-claim batches I checked (B0044, B0214, B0368, B0398, B0134) as a control set. Veneer yield for this lot (0.90) looks normal and in line with other SUP02 lots, so this is a correlational finding based on shared lot usage among the elevated batches — not corroborated by a yield anomaly — but the recurrence of the same specific lot across three of the highest-rate batches, absent from the zero-rate set, is the strongest lead available.

I've submitted `quarantine_batch` proposals for B0030, B0069, and B0002 citing this shared-lot evidence; these are now pending_approval and won't affect what any tool sees until a human approves them. I did not extend this to a supplier-wide corrective action against SUP02, since SUP02's other lots (LOT-MAP-002, -009, -012) show normal yield and aren't implicated — the evidence points specifically at LOT-MAP-007, not the supplier as a whole. B0049 remains the single highest-rate batch but its own material/press-line trail didn't corroborate against other affected batches, so I'm not proposing action on it beyond flagging it as worth a closer look if more claim detail becomes available.
